transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Lee. Well, I’m here because ever since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve just been incredibly keyed up and completely worn down. 

It's really bleeding into everything. I find myself constantly snapping at my wife. And at work—I manage musicians—I've been avoiding calls that I would normally handle immediately. It actually got to the point recently where I nearly let a client's contract fall apart just because I couldn’t think straight. I just really need some help getting a handle on this.
Did these feelings of being keyed up and worn down start around the same time your in-laws moved in, or were you already feeling this way before that happened?

No, I was functioning completely normally before that. I didn't have any of these issues with my work or my mood. It really all started... I'd say within a few weeks of them taking over the house. Before they moved in, I was totally fine.

Aside from the situation with your in-laws, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things in your life—like your health, finances, or other relationships—even when there's no clear reason to?

No, not really. I mean, I have the usual stuff, like making sure the mortgage is paid, but it's not like I'm sitting around worrying about my health or anything like that. It's really just this situation at home that's got me so on edge. Everything else in my life was pretty much on track until they moved in.
Since this all started, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. I'm just... stressed, really. And frustrated. I still enjoy the things I usually like doing, when I actually have the energy for them. It's not a depression thing, it's just this constant tension from the house being so crowded.
Can you tell me exactly how many weeks or months it has been since your in-laws moved in and these symptoms began?
It's been about a month. Yeah, they moved into our home about four weeks ago, and that's exactly when all of this started going on.
Besides the tension at home, has this stress affected your sleep, concentration, or ability to get through your daily responsibilities?

Yeah, it definitely has. I mean, my concentration is shot. At work, I'm an agent for musicians, and... well, I nearly lost a major contract recently because I just couldn't focus. My managing partner actually pulled me aside and questioned whether I could still be trusted to handle the big negotiations right now. That was a huge wake-up call. And at home, it's not just me being stressed—the conflict has gotten so bad that my wife is the one who pushed for us to get outside help. It's just bleeding into everything.
Would you say the level of stress and difficulty you're experiencing feels more intense or disruptive than you'd expect most people to feel in a similar living situation?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't know how other people would handle having their in-laws suddenly move in. I just know that for me... it feels completely overwhelming. 

Maybe someone else could just brush it off or manage the situation better, I don't know. But I can't. I just know that I can't seem to function normally right now, and it's completely derailed my life.
Since this started, have you noticed physical signs of anxiety—like feeling restless, muscle tension, or trouble falling or staying asleep?

I wouldn't say I've had muscle tension or restlessness, really. I mean, my sleep hasn't been great, but it's more just because my mind is racing about everything going on, not so much physical anxiety. I just feel stressed out.

Do you notice this tension, racing thoughts, or difficulty concentrating even when you're away from your in-laws—like during a weekend trip or a full day at work—or does it mostly ease up when you're not around them?

It doesn't really go away, no. Even when I'm at work for the whole day, I'm still just... thinking about it. The stress is always there in the back of my mind. I haven't taken a weekend trip or anything since they moved in, so I don't know about that, but just being out of the house doesn't seem to make a difference. The racing thoughts and the trouble focusing just follow me wherever I go.

You mentioned your wife pushed for you both to get outside help—can you tell me more about how this stress has affected your marriage, such as increased arguments, emotional distance, or other changes in how you two relate to each other?

Well, at home, the conflict between us has just gotten really serious. We're definitely arguing a lot more about the whole living situation, and the tension is just... it's thick. It got bad enough that she finally put her foot down and pushed for us to get outside help. 

But it's not just my marriage that's taking a hit, honestly. It's bleeding into my job, too. I'm a manager for artists, and recently I actually nearly lost a musician's contract because my head just hasn't been in it. My managing partner even sat me down and questioned whether I could still be trusted to handle major negotiations right now. So, yeah, it's affecting my marriage, but it's really derailing everything.

Do you find yourself having intrusive thoughts about the situation, feeling on edge most of the day, or having difficulty functioning to a degree that feels out of proportion to just having in-laws living with you?

I wouldn't say I'm having intrusive thoughts, like where I can't stop thinking about it if I try. And I don't really feel on edge all day, like waiting for something bad to happen. It's more just... a constant stress. I don't know if it's out of proportion or not, honestly. I just know it's really messing up my work and my marriage, but I wouldn't use those specific words to describe it.

Compared to how you've typically handled stressful situations in the past, would you say your current difficulty functioning at work and at home is noticeably more severe or out of proportion, or does it feel like a reasonable reaction to what most people might find quite invasive?

I mean, I don't really know what's normal for this kind of thing. I've handled stress before, sure, but having your in-laws just... move in and take over your space, it's a lot. I don't know if my reaction is out of proportion or if anyone would struggle this much. I just know it's really getting to me, more than I expected.

Has anyone else in your life—like your wife, a close friend, or your managing partner—commented that your reaction to this situation seems more severe than they'd expect, or that you seem to be struggling much more than the circumstances would typically warrant?

No, not really in those words. I mean, my wife obviously knows I'm stressed and that we're fighting a lot, which is why she pushed for the outside help, but she hasn't said I'm... overreacting to them being there, or anything like that. 

And my business partner, he really just cares that my work is slipping. He knows they moved in, but he didn't say my reaction was out of proportion—he just said I need to get my head back in the game and do my job. So no, nobody has specifically told me that I'm struggling more than I should be under the circumstances. They just see that it's causing problems.

Has this situation led to any concrete consequences—like a formal warning or write-up at work, lost income or clients, or any talk of separation or living apart from your wife—as a direct result of how you've been functioning?

Well, at work, it's definitely had consequences. I actually nearly lost a contract for one of my musicians because I was just... so distracted. It was bad enough that my managing partner sat me down and flat-out questioned if I could still be trusted with the major negotiations right now. That was a huge wake-up call, honestly. 

And at home... there hasn't been talk of separation or anything quite that extreme, but the conflict has gotten really serious. It's gotten to the point where my wife is the one who pushed for outside help because we just aren't handling it on our own anymore. So yeah, it's definitely causing real problems.
Has your managing partner given you any formal warning, put you on probation, or indicated your job could be at risk if this continues, or was it more of a verbal concern without formal action?

No, it wasn't anything formal like probation or a written warning. He didn't say I was going to be fired. It was just a very serious conversation where he told me he was worried about my focus and whether I should be handling the big negotiations right now. So it was more of a verbal concern, but coming from him, it felt pretty significant.
